title: The Nations of the World
aka: descendants of Shem, Ham and Japheth
lead: Genesis 10 traces every known people to one family, the sons of Noah, and the rest of the Bible keeps that whole world in view: Abraham's blessing is for "all the clans of the earth" (Genesis 12:3), the prophets address the nations, and Revelation sees people "from every nation, tribe, people and language" (Revelation 7:9).

sections.b: Deuteronomy 32:8 says God "marked out the peoples' borders" when he split up the children of Adam, and Jewish tradition counted seventy nations, as Genesis 10 lists seventy names. Paul tells the Athenians that God "made from one man every nation" (Acts 17:26). The list in Acts 2:9–11 of peoples who heard the apostles at Pentecost may deliberately echo Genesis 10. The idea that Noah's curse (Genesis 9:25) fell on Africans was a later misreading used to defend slavery; the text curses Canaan.
sections.refs: Genesis 10:1–32; Genesis 12:3; Deuteronomy 32:8; Acts 17:26; Acts 2:9–11; Revelation 7:9; Genesis 9:25
